title: Keep the Lifetime ISA for new savers
name: Keep the Lifetime ISA for new savers
noun: keeping the Lifetime ISA for new savers
headline: Keep the Lifetime ISA. Costs £0.1bn in 2029-30.
description: From April 2029 a new First Time Buyer ISA replaces the Lifetime ISA for new savers, with a 25% bonus towards a first home up to £450,000. The change saves money from 2029-30. Switch this on to keep the Lifetime ISA open to new savers instead.

baselinePolicy.text: A First Time Buyer ISA replaces the Lifetime ISA for new savers from 6 April 2029 (Table 6.1 line 38).

source.quote: This measure introduces a new First Time Buyer ISA, replacing the Lifetime ISA for new customers.

alreadyIncludes: A First Time Buyer ISA replaces the Lifetime ISA for new savers from 6 April 2029 (Table 6.1 line 38).

lines.title: First Time Buyer ISA: Introduce a new ISA for first-time buyers, replacing the Lifetime ISA for new savers from 6 April 2029

rawSource.note: Reversal on the spending side: the Treasury’s costing with the sign kept (a line that reduced borrowing is spending the reversal adds back; a line that cost money is spending the reversal saves).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
